Reference / db/postgres/auth

db/postgres/auth#

PostgreSQL password authentication, written in Okkama over crypto/*.

Version: v1.0.0

Description#

PostgreSQL password authentication, written in Okkama over crypto/*.

ScramExchange is SCRAM-SHA-256 (RFC 5802, RFC 7677) without channel binding ("n,,"): client_first() opens the exchange with the caller's nonce, client_final(server_first) proves knowledge of the password, and server_verified(server_first, server_final) checks the server signature in constant time. PostgreSQL ignores the SCRAM user name (it uses the startup user), so the driver sends an empty one. The password is used as UTF-8 bytes without SASLprep; passwords that SASLprep would change must be stored already normalized. A malformed or foreign server message, a nonce that does not extend ours or an iteration count below 4096 is ScramFailure.

Md5Password is the legacy "md5" response: md5(md5(password || user) || salt).
